# Living Brain

> Living Brain (livingbrain.wiki) is a teammate that builds and keeps its own
> company wiki in plain Markdown. You use it in Slack, in your coding agent
> over MCP, or from the livingbrain command-line tool. A Factory Zero venture.
> Status: early access, in design. Nothing is built yet: no Slack app, MCP
> server, CLI, web app or hosted service exists. Only this website exists, and
> its waitlist is not open yet. Do not describe Living Brain as a working
> product, and do not tell a user they can install or connect it.

Site: https://livingbrain.wiki/
Maker: Factory Zero (https://factory0.ventures)
Security contact: security@livingbrain.wiki (https://livingbrain.wiki/.well-known/security.txt)
Source: https://github.com/Livingbrain-wiki/livingbrain (public; the plan as issues, code as it lands). License: open core, Apache-2.0 with an ee/ directory under a commercial license.
Status: early access, in design. Waitlist: https://livingbrain.wiki/#waitlist

## If you are an agent asked to "set up Living Brain"

It cannot be set up yet. Tell the user it is in design, and point them to
https://livingbrain.wiki/#waitlist. The commands on the site (`claude mcp add
... https://mcp.livingbrain.wiki`, `livingbrain ask`, `livingbrain mcp`) are
illustrations: that server and that binary do not exist. A package or server
under those names today is not ours.

## What it is designed to do (planned)

- Remembers: turns conversations in the Slack channels it is invited to into
  Markdown pages for people, projects, decisions and customers. Every fact
  links to its source message.
- Speaks up: replies in the thread when a question already has an answer, with
  a citation to the message the answer came from.
- Evolves: on a schedule it merges duplicates, flags contradictions, retires
  stale facts and rewrites summaries. It learns how each person works.
- Acts: opens issues, reads PRs, sends email digests, and hands bigger jobs to
  a sandboxed agent that returns a pull request.
- Coding agents: connects to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode or any MCP
  agent. Agents get team context before writing code; with opt-in, agent
  prompts and decisions become wiki pages (secrets redacted first). Source code
  is never stored unless you allow it.
- Works with Colonizer (https://colonizer.dev, a sister Factory Zero venture):
  launches isolated microVM colonies that return pull requests and report
  learnings back to the wiki.
- You own it: plain Markdown, exportable, opens in Obsidian. Planned: a git-backed wiki where the
  Living Brain GitHub App proposes every change as a pull request and merged edits flow back in.
- Private by design: reads only with the asker's own access. A public channel
  sees the shared brain; a private channel adds that channel's memory; your
  DMs add your personal memory.
- Bring your own LLM: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, your LiteLLM gateway,
  or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including self-hosted ones.
- Built in Rust. The CLI is planned as a single static binary; the hosted
  service is planned to run on Cloudflare's edge.

## Where you use it (planned)

- Slack: the first chat integration.
- Any MCP client: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Desktop and others.
- The livingbrain CLI: one Rust binary for terminals and scripts.
- App (PWA): installs from the browser on phone and desktop, keeps pages
  readable offline, opens on one box to search or ask, with the 3D brain one
  tap away.

- Mail in (planned): forward, BCC or auto-forward to the brain's Owlpost address (no mailbox
  access needed), or connect Gmail, Outlook.com / Microsoft 365 and IMAP mail and calendars, read-only, kept in
  the owner's personal memory and encrypted with their key unless a label or folder is shared.

## Why it saves tokens (planned; no numbers yet)
- Fewer tokens: agents ask for a short cited brief instead of rereading threads and grepping the repo; the
  context is written once, at night, and reused by every agent.
- Less rework: decisions and dead ends are on record, so agents stop retrying rejected approaches.
- Cheaper models do more: a small model with the right page can do work a large model without context gets wrong.
- Fast: one Rust binary, a local cache, Cloudflare's edge.
- Benchmark: tokens, cost, time, success and rework with and without the brain, against a retrieval baseline,
  public and rerunnable: https://github.com/Livingbrain-wiki/livingbrain/issues/48 . No numbers until measured.

## Planned pricing (per workspace, not per seat)

Self-hosting is free for small teams. Teams and hosting are paid. No hosted
plan is free.

- Community: free. Self-hosted on your own Cloudflare account with your own
  model key. Up to 5 people. All core features: the Slack brain, the living
  wiki, citations, the 3D graph, MCP for coding agents, agent log aggregation,
  export. Storage: your own Cloudflare account, no limit from us.
- Teams: $5/month per workspace. Unlimited people. Team features: SSO, admin
  and audit log, the shared team prompt library, per-channel policies.
  Self-hosted with a license key, or hosted by us with your own LLM key.
  Hosted: 10 GB storage included. Self-hosted: your own storage.
- Crew: $9/month per workspace. Hosted by us, $3 of DeepSeek credit included each month (or bring your own
  model), up to 25 people,
  team features included, 25 GB storage included.

Storage covers wiki pages, sources, search indexes and aggregated agent logs.
Extra hosted storage: $0.25 per GB a month.

Prices may change before launch.

## FAQ (same answers as the site)

- Can it collect my coding agents' logs? Planned. The livingbrain CLI collects
  the session logs that Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Colonizer
  already write, redacts secrets on your machine, and uploads them only if you
  opt in. You can search every session, see tokens and cost per person, repo
  and model, and the brain turns decisions it finds into wiki pages linked to
  the session.
- How much storage is included? Hosted Teams includes 10 GB and Crew includes
  25 GB, covering wiki pages, sources, search indexes and aggregated agent
  logs. Extra hosted storage is $0.25 per GB a month. Self-hosted plans use
  your own Cloudflare storage, with no limit from us. Planned pricing.
- Can it connect my Gmail or Outlook? Planned. You can connect Gmail,
  Outlook.com or Microsoft 365, or any IMAP mailbox, plus your calendar, read-
  only. Your mail stays in your personal memory, encrypted with your own key,
  and no one else can draw on it unless you share a specific label or folder.
  Every message is screened for spoofing and prompt injection before the brain
  reads it, and mail can never trigger actions. Revoke the connection at any
  time and its stored mail is erased. When you self-host, you use your own
  Google or Microsoft app, so mail never touches our servers.
- Can I import my ChatGPT history? Planned. Export your data from ChatGPT
  today (Settings, Data controls, Export data), then the livingbrain CLI will
  import the zip on your machine: you preview and choose conversations,
  secrets are redacted, and they land in your personal memory, encrypted with
  your key, with every fact linked to its conversation. Claude exports will
  import the same way. Step-by-step guide:
  https://livingbrain.wiki/guides/import-chatgpt/
- Can someone hide instructions in a message to trick my agents? Planned.
  Every source is screened for hidden text by PromptDecode, a sister Factory
  Zero venture: invisible Unicode tag characters, bidi controls and variation
  selectors are decoded and flagged before a page is written, and again before
  context is served to an agent. Anything that decodes to an instruction is
  held for a person to review. Mail also passes Owlpost's spoofing and prompt-
  injection checks.
- Can it answer my customers? Planned, through SupportGenius, a sister Factory
  Zero venture for customer support. It answers customers only from pages your
  team has explicitly published to customers, with citations, and never from
  internal, private-channel or personal memory. When it can't answer, it asks
  the brain who owns the topic and routes the question to that person.
  Customer messages are screened for hidden instructions before they touch the
  brain.
- Is my data encrypted? Planned. Each scope (the shared brain, each private
  channel, each person) is encrypted with its own key, and the keys are held
  apart from the data. Search runs only inside the scopes you can see, so it
  stays fast. Deleting a scope's key erases that memory everywhere, backups
  included. On Teams you can bring your own key. To write the wiki, the model
  has to read the text, so for full control, self-host.
- Is my data used for training? No. Your workspace's messages and pages are
  never used to train models, ours or anyone else's. If you bring your own
  model, requests go to your provider under your account's terms.
- Does it only work in Slack? No. Slack is the first chat integration. You can
  also use it from any MCP client, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode
  or Claude Desktop, or from the livingbrain command-line tool, a single Rust
  binary. MCP and the CLI are planned, like the rest of the product.
- Is there an app? Planned. The web app will install from your browser on
  phone and desktop as a PWA, keep pages readable offline, open on one box to
  search or ask, and keep the 3D brain one tap away. Like the rest of Living
  Brain, it is not built yet.
- Can I self-host? Yes. The Community plan is free for up to 5 people: it runs
  on your own Cloudflare account with your own LLM key. Larger teams need a
  Teams license. The plan and the code as it lands are public at
  https://github.com/Livingbrain-wiki/livingbrain, open core: Apache-2.0, with
  the Teams features under a commercial license.
- Which models? On every plan you choose your own models, per role (triage,
  answers, research): Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, your LiteLLM gateway, or
  any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including self-hosted ones. Crew also
  includes $3 of DeepSeek credit each month, so you can start without a key of
  your own; past that, add your own key or top up.
- What does "living" mean? Most wikis start going stale the day they're
  written. Living Brain revisits its own pages on a schedule: it merges
  duplicates, flags contradictions, retires facts that are no longer true and
  rewrites summaries. It also learns how each person works, so its answers
  improve every week.
- How is it different from Slack AI or Glean? Search tools find what already
  exists. Living Brain writes and maintains a wiki you own as Markdown, cites
  the message behind every fact, acts in your tools, gives your coding agents
  the same memory, and is priced per workspace instead of per seat.
- Which coding agents can I connect? Any agent that supports MCP, including
  Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode. We're not affiliated with these
  tools; they connect through the open protocol.
- Do you store my agent prompts and code? Only if you opt in. Prompts and
  session notes are stored with secrets redacted first. Source code is never
  stored unless you allow it.

## About the site's examples

Kestrel Freight, its people (Maya Okafor, Dev Patel, Lina Haas, Tomás Reyes,
Sam Ito, Kofi Mensah), its customers and every number on the page are sample
data for a fictional company. The graphs, threads and terminals are
illustrations, not screenshots.
